panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Histology image from enucleated eye of Lowe syndrome patient showing corneal opacification with fibrovascular proliferation in the subepithelial region, consistent with corneal ischemia as described in the caption. B: Histology image showing anterior chamber abnormalities in Lowe syndrome, including dense fibrous tissue covering the angle, peripheral anterior synechiae, ectropion uvea, and iris stromal atrophy. C: Histology image showing an underdeveloped and atrophic ciliary body with peripheral staphyloma in Lowe syndrome. D: Histology image showing optic nerve pathology in Lowe syndrome including loss of retinal ganglion cell layer, retinal gliosis, and glaucomatous cupping of the optic nerve head.

(C) Ciliary body is underdeveloped and atrophic with peripheral staphyloma. Scale bar 0.5 mm. (D) Optic nerve shows loss of retinal ganglion cell layer, retinal gliosis, and cupping of optic nerve head. Scale bar 0.5 mm.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, C). A: Immunofluorescence of patient-derived LS renal cells showing impaired primary ciliation assembly, confirming a pathological mechanism associated with Lowe Syndrome. C: Immunofluorescence visualizing primary cilia components (Ac-Tub, PC2) in LS-relevant genetic models (OCLN/OCRL deficiency), showing the failure of ciliogenesis.
panels.attribution_text: Hsieh et al. Kidney-differentiated cells derived from Lowe Syndrome patient's iPSCs show ciliogenesis defects and Six2 retention at the Golgi complex.. PloS one 2018. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0192635. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: LS renal cells show defects in primary cilia assembly. Ciliogenesis in kidney-differentiated cells was induced as described in Materials and methods. A and C. Primary cilia (PC) presence was investigated in renal-differentiated (A) and HK2 (C) cells by indirect immunofluorescence using anti-acetylated tubulin (Ac-Tub, green), anti-pericentrin-2 (PC2, red) antibodies. DAPI staining (blue) was performed to highlight nucleus position. Scale bar: 10μm. B and D. The percentage of cells displaying PC was determined for normal and LS renal differentiated (B) and HK2 (D) cells. Statistical significance of difference between means was assessed by using the student t-test (**: p<0.05).

A: Brain MRI shows characteristic cystic and degenerative changes (ventriculomegaly, white matter shrinkage, cerebellar hypoplasia) consistent with Lowe syndrome in a child. B: Kidney histology shows focal fibrosis and cellular infiltration, representing renal pathology consistent with Lowe syndrome.
